messages:
Anna: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands runtime roadmap — can someone clarify how we prioritize kernel work vs batching/caching efforts?
Raj: Short answer: we prioritize regressions impacting P95 latency first, then cost wins. Longer answer below.
Anna: thanks — can you expand on the tradeoffs?
Raj: Sure. Kernel work (fusion, memory layout, custom attention) yields deterministic latency improvements across requests but has higher dev + review cost. Batching/caching yields big $/token wins for high-concurrency customers and is faster to iterate.
Priya: To add: kernel changes need model-specific perf validation and sometimes infra changes (driver/kernel flags). So rollout cadence is slower.
Marco: Also worth noting: kernel wins are sticky — once landed all tenants benefit. Batching/caching changes can be targeted per-customer or per-route which helps staged rollouts.
Anna: Is there a rubric we use to decide? e.g., >10% P95 or >30% cost reduction?
Raj: We use three criteria currently: 1) Customer impact (latency or cost), 2) Risk & rollability, 3) Implementation effort. Thresholds are soft — e.g., >8% P95 or >20% cost for top customers triggers kernel consideration.
Olivia: Ops question: when kernel work lands, what are our rollback knobs?
Raj: We keep dual-kernel artifacts and runtime selection flags. We can route traffic back to previous kernel variant per-pool. Also fallback to a compatible quantized variant if needed.
Priya: On batching: the Optimize team has an experiment that auto-tunes batching window per-tenant. Early results: 18-22% cost reduction on chat workloads with <5ms added median latency.
Anna: Nice — where can I see the experiment data?
Priya: Link: https://docs.redwood.ai/optimize/experiments/auto-batch-2026 — internal only. I'll add a short summary to the post-all-hands notes.
Anna: Will kernel changes invalidate caching layers or KV prefixes?
Raj: Generally no for logical prefixes. But some kernel-level memory layout changes required a small bump to KV serialization on a past test; we kept backward compatibility. We'll call out any cache-format change well before rollout.
Marco: Action item: Raj + Priya to create a short playbook for PMs/SEs describing when to push kernel vs batching, and what to expect in canaries.
Raj: I'll draft it, target EOW.
Olivia: Can we add a checklist for private deployments? Some customers asked if on-prem stacks will need manual kernel upgrades.
Raj: Yes — private customers must opt-in for kernel updates. Playbook will include steps and version matrix.
SRE Bot: deploy-bot started canary for kernel-v3 on pool:dedicated-us-west-2 at 1909001280 — 10% traffic.
Priya: Ping me if canary shows CPU jitter — auto-batcher might interact oddly with kernel scheduling.
Anna: Thanks all. Quick ask from leadership: can we include expected timelines (rough) in the playbook so sales/CS can set expectations?
Marco: Good call. Raj: please include an ETA range (fast/normal/slow).
Raj: Will do.
Anna: One last Q — are we measuring quality/regression risk from kernel vs batching? how do we roll back if generations change?
Priya: We tie quality checks to our eval harness. Kernel changes run the same evals plus a targeted prompt suite. If diffs exceed thresholds we fail the rollout. We also have staged fallback to the previous model+kernel pairing.
Anna: Awesome. thanks for the quick clarifications.
Raj: Happy to follow-up in more detail in eng-runtime channel or 1:1s.
Anna: If folks have small follow-ups, drop them here and we'll consolidate into the playbook. :white_check_mark:
Priya: I'll paste experiment graphs in eng-runtime tomorrow.
Olivia: Adding request: add a short FAQ entry about "will my private infra need downtime for kernel upgrades?"
Raj: Not usually; in-place live swap for most dedicated pools. We'll document exceptions.
Anna: closing this thread after we get the playbook draft. thanks everyone!
